about.tool: A brush pen or a flexible pointed nib: press on the way down, lift to a hairline on the way up.
about.slant: Strongly slanted: about 25° from upright, as on the exemplar a-z (writers range from upright to about 30°).
about.proportions: A small x-height with long, narrow loops: ascenders about twice the x-height, descenders about one and a half; compressed letters (m and n stems half an x-height apart); capitals as tall as the ascenders.
about.features: Small letters are built from eight basic strokes (entry upstroke, downstroke, underturn, overturn, compound curve, oval, ascending and descending loop), with an entry hairline from the baseline and an exit hairline; long narrow loops; a looped r and z, a tall s; a bouncing baseline, where letters rise and dip a little.
about.history: A 21st-century practice, not one fixed script: it loosens the rules of copperplate and pointed-pen script. This model follows one exemplar, a modern calligraphy alphabet; the bounce of the sheet is kept only in r, s and o, joins and flourishes are left out, and the capitals and figures, which the sheet does not show, are simple open forms in the same style.
